newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Aramco to market Shaybah crude as blend - MEES.
newsitem.headline: Aramco to market Shaybah crude as blend - MEES.

text.p: Saudi Aramco will market crude from its Shaybah field development as a blend of Shaybah and existing Arabian Extra Light output rather than as a separate stream, the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) reported on Monday.

The 500,000 barrels per day (bpd) Shaybah field, due onstream in June 1998, was originally to be marketed as a distinct grade, though the cost of building new dedicated export facilities for the field had led to a change in Aramco planning.

Shaybah has a higher API gravity level and lower sulphur content than the proposed new blend, but Aramco had "decided that the added investment requirement and extra administrative cost outweighed the potential revenue advantages associated with selling Shaybah as a distinct stream," MEES reported.
First exports of the three-stream blend from the Gulf Ras Tanura export terminal are expected in third quarter 1998.
Arabian Extra Light has been running at around 950,000 bpd, made up of 650,000 bpd from the Abqaiq field and 300,000 bpd from Berri. Aramco produces eight million bpd.
The new Shaybah-Abqaiq-Berri blend is expected to have an API of 38.4 degrees, compared to Shaybah's own API of 41.6 and the Extra Light stream which ranges between 36 and 37 API.
A blend sample consisting of 37.04 percent of Shaybah stream, 22.22 percent of Berri and 40.74 percent of Abqaiq crude showed the stream would have a sulphur content of 1.16 percent.
Aramco term customers had received an initial quality sample from a Shaybah production well and the state firm had prepared a comprehensine assay of the new Shaybah blend, MEES said.
Aramco was expected to cut back production of its main 5.1-5.2 million bpd Arab Light stream once Shaybah came on stream in order to maintain its OPEC quota of eight million bpd.
